# DAGTaxonomy { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy }

```python
DAGTaxonomy(n_nodes, diversity, children, parents, roots, leaves)
```

A navigable DAG taxonomy extracted from embedding space.

Provides lattice operations for exploring hierarchical relationships:
- Find ancestors/descendants of a concept
- Find common ancestors between concepts
- Find paths through the taxonomy
- Identify convergence points (abstract attractors)

The taxonomy is a true lattice (not a tree) - nodes can have multiple
parents, enabling multiple inheritance and diamond patterns.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name      | Type                                                                                                                                        | Description                                           |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| n_nodes   | [int](`int`)                                                                                                                                | Total number of nodes in the taxonomy                 |
| diversity | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`)                                                                                                    | Neighbor diversity score for each node                |
| children  | [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[int](`int`), [List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[int](`int`), [float](`float`), [float](`float`)\]\]\] | Dict mapping node → list of (child, similarity, gap)  |
| parents   | [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[int](`int`), [List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[int](`int`), [float](`float`), [float](`float`)\]\]\] | Dict mapping node → list of (parent, similarity, gap) |
| roots     | [List](`typing.List`)\[[int](`int`)\]                                                                                                       | Nodes with no parents (most general concepts)         |
| leaves    | [List](`typing.List`)\[[int](`int`)\]                                                                                                       | Nodes with no children (most specific concepts)       |

## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> from dyf import build_dag_taxonomy
>>>
>>> taxonomy = build_dag_taxonomy(embeddings, verbose=True)
>>> print(taxonomy.summary())
>>>
>>> # Find ancestors of a concept
>>> ancestors = taxonomy.get_ancestors(node_idx, max_depth=5)
>>>
>>> # Find common ancestors between two concepts
>>> common = taxonomy.get_common_ancestors(idx_a, idx_b)
>>>
>>> # Get convergence points (highly connected abstract concepts)
>>> hubs = taxonomy.get_convergence_points(min_parents=10)

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [get_all_paths](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_all_paths) | Find all paths from start to end. |
| [get_ancestors](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_ancestors) | Get all ancestors of a node (transitive closure upward). |
| [get_children](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_children) | Get direct children of a node. |
| [get_common_ancestors](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_common_ancestors) | Find common ancestors of two nodes. |
| [get_convergence_points](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_convergence_points) | Find convergence points (nodes with many incoming edges). |
| [get_descendants](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_descendants) | Get all descendants of a node (transitive closure downward). |
| [get_diamond_patterns](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_diamond_patterns) | Find diamond patterns (A → B, A → C, B → D, C → D). |
| [get_divergence_points](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_divergence_points) | Find divergence points (nodes with many outgoing edges). |
| [get_lowest_common_ancestors](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_lowest_common_ancestors) | Find lowest common ancestors (LCAs) of two nodes. |
| [get_node_depth](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_node_depth) | Get the depth of a node (distance from nearest root). |
| [get_parents](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_parents) | Get direct parents of a node. |
| [get_path](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_path) | Find a path from start to end (following parent→child direction). |
| [summary](#dyf.DAGTaxonomy.summary) | Return summary statistics. |

### get_all_paths { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_all_paths }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_all_paths(start, end, max_depth=10)
```

Find all paths from start to end.

In a lattice, there can be multiple paths between nodes.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type         | Description                  | Default    |
|-----------|--------------|------------------------------|------------|
| start     | [int](`int`) | Starting node (more general) | _required_ |
| end       | [int](`int`) | Ending node (more specific)  | _required_ |
| max_depth | [int](`int`) | Maximum path length          | `10`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                           | Description                                              |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [List](`typing.List`)\[[List](`typing.List`)\[[int](`int`)\]\] | List of paths, where each path is a list of node indices |

### get_ancestors { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_ancestors }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_ancestors(node, max_depth=10)
```

Get all ancestors of a node (transitive closure upward).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type         | Description               | Default    |
|-----------|--------------|---------------------------|------------|
| node      | [int](`int`) | Starting node index       | _required_ |
| max_depth | [int](`int`) | Maximum depth to traverse | `10`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                      |
|--------|--------------|----------------------------------|
|        | [set](`set`) | Set of all ancestor node indices |

### get_children { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_children }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_children(node)
```

Get direct children of a node.

### get_common_ancestors { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_common_ancestors }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_common_ancestors(node_a, node_b, max_depth=10)
```

Find common ancestors of two nodes.

In a lattice (vs tree), there can be multiple common ancestors,
not just a single LCA.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type         | Description             | Default    |
|-----------|--------------|-------------------------|------------|
| node_a    | [int](`int`) | First node index        | _required_ |
| node_b    | [int](`int`) | Second node index       | _required_ |
| max_depth | [int](`int`) | Maximum depth to search | `10`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                    |
|--------|--------------|--------------------------------|
|        | [set](`set`) | Set of common ancestor indices |

### get_convergence_points { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_convergence_points }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_convergence_points(min_parents=5)
```

Find convergence points (nodes with many incoming edges).

These are abstract concepts where many paths converge.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type         | Description                          | Default   |
|-------------|--------------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
| min_parents | [int](`int`) | Minimum number of parents to qualify | `5`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                           | Description                                                         |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[int](`int`), [int](`int`)\]\] | List of (node_idx, parent_count) tuples, sorted by count descending |

### get_diamond_patterns { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_diamond_patterns }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_diamond_patterns(limit=100)
```

Find diamond patterns (A → B, A → C, B → D, C → D).

Diamonds indicate multiple inheritance / non-tree structure.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type         | Description                          | Default   |
|--------|--------------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
| limit  | [int](`int`) | Maximum number of diamonds to return | `100`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                                       | Description                               |
|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
|        | [List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[int](`int`), [int](`int`), [int](`int`), [int](`int`)\]\] | List of (top, left, right, bottom) tuples |

### get_divergence_points { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_divergence_points }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_divergence_points(min_children=5)
```

Find divergence points (nodes with many outgoing edges).

These are branching hubs where paths diverge.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type         | Description                           | Default   |
|--------------|--------------|---------------------------------------|-----------|
| min_children | [int](`int`) | Minimum number of children to qualify | `5`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                           | Description                                                        |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [List](`typing.List`)\[[Tuple](`typing.Tuple`)\[[int](`int`), [int](`int`)\]\] | List of (node_idx, child_count) tuples, sorted by count descending |

### get_lowest_common_ancestors { #dyf.DAGTaxonomy.get_lowest_common_ancestors }

```python
DAGTaxonomy.get_lowest_common_ancestors(node_a, node_b, max_depth=10)
```

Find lowest common ancestors (LCAs) of two nodes.

Returns ancestors that are common to both nodes but have no
descendants that are also common ancestors.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type         | Description             | Default    |
|-----------|--------------|-------------------------|------------|
| node_a    | [int](`int`) | First node index        | _required_ |
| node_b    | [int](`int`) | Second node index       | _required_ |
| max_depth | [int](`int`) | Maximum depth to search | `10`       |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                  | Description                                        |
|--------|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [List](`typing.List`)\[[int](`int`)\] | List of LCA indices (may be multiple in a lattice) |
